title: Add an interactive pre-refine step to the SDLC pipeline
summary: Architecture analysis for adding a conversational pre-refine phase where a human and Claude collaborate to produce a clear requirements document before the refine phase begins. The pre-refine step is fundamentally different from existing phases: it is human-driven and conversational rather than agent-driven with HITL gates. The recommended approach uses the existing egg-sdlc CLI to host the interactive session, adds a new PRE_REFINE pipeline phase, and stores the approved requirements document at .egg-state/drafts/{identifier}-requirements.md. The approved document replaces the original issue body/prompt as input to the refine phase.

problem_statement.description: The SDLC pipeline currently starts at the refine phase, where an agent autonomously analyzes an issue and produces an analysis document. If the original issue/prompt is poorly defined, the refine agent may produce a low-quality analysis, leading to wasted cycles through multiple HITL revision loops or cascading misunderstandings through plan and implement. There is no structured mechanism for a human to collaboratively clarify requirements before autonomous work begins.
goals: Add a conversational pre-refine step where human and Claude collaborate to produce a clear requirements document
The step must be interactive and free-form (back-and-forth conversation, not structured HITL checkboxes)
Support both issue mode (GitHub issue) and local mode (no GitHub)
Produce a single requirements document with: problem statement, functional requirements, constraints, acceptance criteria, and any other context
Human must explicitly approve the requirements document before advancing to refine
The approved document replaces the original issue body/prompt as the direct input to the refine phase
In issue mode, update the GitHub issue description with the approved requirements document
No codebase interaction during pre-refine — purely requirements-focused

pipeline_phases.mechanism: PipelinePhase enum defines exactly 4 phases: REFINE, PLAN, IMPLEMENT, PR. Each pipeline tracks current_phase and per-phase execution state.
pipeline_phases.constraint: Adding a new phase requires updating the enum, phase transitions, phase permissions, prompt building, HITL handling, and CLI phase detection.

phase_transitions.mechanism: PHASE_TRANSITIONS dict maps each phase to valid successor phases. REFINE -> [PLAN, IMPLEMENT] (short-circuit), PLAN -> [IMPLEMENT], IMPLEMENT -> [PR], PR -> [] (terminal). Separate LOCAL_PHASE_TRANSITIONS map exists but is currently identical.
phase_transitions.constraint: Adding PRE_REFINE requires a new transition: PRE_REFINE -> [REFINE].

pipeline_orchestration.mechanism: _run_pipeline() is the main background thread. It loops through phases, spawning agent containers, running review cycles, and pausing for HITL approval. Each phase runs one or more agent containers via _spawn_and_wait().
pipeline_orchestration.key_detail: All existing phases follow the pattern: spawn non-interactive agent container in --print mode -> wait for exit -> read artifacts -> optionally review -> HITL gate. Pre-refine breaks this pattern because it requires an interactive, conversational session rather than a headless agent run.

hitl_handling.mechanism: handle_hitl_checkpoint() presents a 5-option menu when pipeline pauses: edit with $EDITOR, launch Claude, approve, provide feedback, cancel. This is the closest existing infrastructure to an interactive step but is post-phase (runs after agent completes), not in-place-of a phase.
hitl_handling.key_detail: Option 2 ('Launch Claude for AI-assisted editing') already spawns an interactive Claude Code session with context about the current draft. This pattern could be adapted for pre-refine.

cli_pipeline_watch.mechanism: watch_pipeline() connects to SSE stream and monitors events. When pipeline status is 'awaiting_human', it calls handle_hitl_checkpoint(). The watch loop handles reconnection and terminal states.
cli_pipeline_watch.key_detail: The watch loop is where the egg-sdlc CLI interacts with the human. Pre-refine must integrate here.

prompt_building.mechanism: _build_phase_prompt() constructs phase-specific prompts for agent containers. Refine prompt includes the issue body/prompt and asks for analysis. Plan prompt includes the prior analysis.
prompt_building.key_detail: The refine prompt currently receives the raw issue body/prompt. Pre-refine would replace this with the approved requirements document.

phase_permissions.mechanism: Each phase defines allowed/blocked operations and file patterns. Refine allows gh issue comment/edit, git push for state files, and egg-contract operations.
phase_permissions.key_detail: Pre-refine would need minimal permissions — no code changes, no PRs. Potentially only needs to write the requirements document to .egg-state/drafts/.

local_mode_input.mechanism: run_local_mode() already has a basic interactive prompt: 'What would you like to build or change?' and 'Any specific files?'. This input becomes pipeline.prompt which is passed directly to the refine agent.
local_mode_input.key_detail: Pre-refine for local mode would replace this simple prompt with a richer conversational requirements gathering session.

draft_management.mechanism: _get_draft_path() returns phase-specific paths. Refine: {prefix}-analysis.md, Plan: {prefix}-plan.md. The prefix is pipeline_id (local) or issue_number (issue mode).
draft_management.key_detail: Pre-refine would add a new draft type: {prefix}-requirements.md.

approaches.name: New PRE_REFINE pipeline phase with interactive Claude session (recommended)
approaches.description: Add PRE_REFINE as a first-class pipeline phase. When the pipeline enters pre-refine, the orchestrator pauses (AWAITING_HUMAN) and the egg-sdlc CLI launches an interactive Claude Code session configured with a requirements-gathering system prompt. Claude asks probing questions, the human responds conversationally, and together they produce a requirements document. When the human approves, the CLI writes the document to .egg-state/drafts/{identifier}-requirements.md, resolves the HITL decision, and the pipeline advances to REFINE with the requirements document as input.
pros: Clean separation of concerns: pre-refine is its own phase with its own state tracking
Fits naturally into the existing phase lifecycle: status tracking, SSE events, visualization all work
The interactive Claude session is already a proven pattern (HITL option 2 uses the same mechanism)
Pipeline can be restarted/resumed from pre-refine if interrupted
Phase permissions can restrict pre-refine to only requirements document writes
Pipeline visualization correctly shows PRE_REFINE as a distinct step
DAG visualization and SSE stream events work without special casing
cons: New enum value touches many code paths (phase transition, prompt building, phase detection, etc.)
Existing pipelines created before the change won't have PRE_REFINE state
The interactive session breaks the existing pattern of non-interactive agent containers
Requires careful handling of the phase in issue mode (no container to spawn for pre-refine)

approaches.name: Pre-pipeline CLI step (no new phase)
approaches.description: Instead of adding a new pipeline phase, run the requirements gathering session entirely within the egg-sdlc CLI before creating the pipeline. The CLI launches an interactive Claude session, produces a requirements document, and then creates the pipeline with the requirements as the prompt/issue body. No orchestrator changes needed.
pros: No changes to the orchestrator, phase enum, or pipeline state
Simpler implementation — entirely in the CLI layer
No new phase to handle in visualization, SSE events, etc.
cons: Requirements gathering is invisible to the pipeline — no state tracking, no restart capability
Cannot skip pre-refine for well-defined issues (always runs or needs an explicit flag to skip)
In issue mode, the requirements doc exists only as the modified issue body — no separate artifact
Cannot be monitored via SSE stream or visualized in the DAG
If the CLI crashes during requirements gathering, all work is lost (no checkpoint)
Not composable with headless/CI pipeline triggers — only works with interactive CLI

approaches.name: Reuse HITL gate at refine phase start
approaches.description: Instead of a new phase, add an optional HITL gate at the start of the refine phase. When the pipeline reaches REFINE, it immediately pauses (AWAITING_HUMAN) and presents the original issue/prompt for collaborative refinement. The human uses the existing HITL menu (edit, Claude, approve, feedback) to produce a requirements document. On approval, the refine agent runs with the refined input.
pros: No new phase — reuses existing HITL infrastructure
Minimal orchestrator changes — just add a pre-agent HITL gate to refine
Backward compatible — gate can be optional (controlled by config)
Works with existing SSE events and visualization (shows as AWAITING_HUMAN in refine phase)
cons: Conflates two distinct concepts (requirements gathering vs. analysis review) in one phase
The HITL menu is designed for post-phase artifact review, not conversational requirements gathering
No separate requirements artifact — the refined input replaces the original prompt in-place
The refine phase HITL gate (post-agent) becomes confusable with the pre-agent gate
Pipeline status shows 'refine/awaiting_human' for both pre-refine requirements AND post-refine review, making it hard to tell them apart in monitoring

recommended_approach.name: New PRE_REFINE pipeline phase with interactive Claude session
justification: A new phase provides clean separation of concerns. Pre-refine is conceptually distinct from analysis (refine): it's human-driven requirements gathering, not agent-driven codebase analysis. Modeling it as its own phase makes this distinction explicit in the system's state machine.

The existing HITL infrastructure (decision queue, _launch_claude() in sdlc_hitl.py) already supports the interactive Claude session pattern needed for pre-refine. The main new work is: (1) the requirements-gathering system prompt, (2) writing the requirements document, and (3) plumbing the new phase through the orchestrator.

Approach B (pre-pipeline CLI step) loses state tracking and restart capability. If the user's terminal disconnects during a long requirements session, all work is lost. With a phase, the pipeline knows it's in pre-refine and can resume.

Approach C (HITL gate at refine start) conflates two different HITL pauses in the same phase. Pipeline monitoring cannot distinguish 'waiting for requirements' from 'waiting for analysis review'. A separate phase makes pipeline state unambiguous.

The issue explicitly states pre-refine should work in both local and issue modes. A first-class phase naturally supports both through the same orchestration loop, while Approach B would require separate handling for each mode.

The enum change (adding PRE_REFINE) is the largest risk, but the codebase already handled adding the PR phase and the short-circuit REFINE -> IMPLEMENT transition. The pattern for adding phases is well-established.

technical_decisions.decision: Model pre-refine as a first-class pipeline phase (PRE_REFINE)
technical_decisions.rationale: Clean state machine semantics. Pipeline status unambiguously shows whether the system is gathering requirements (pre_refine) vs. running analysis (refine). Enables state tracking, restart from pre-refine, SSE events, and visualization. The alternative (pre-pipeline CLI step) loses all observability.
alternatives_considered: Pre-pipeline CLI step — rejected: no state tracking, no restart, invisible to monitoring
HITL gate at refine start — rejected: conflates two HITL pauses in one phase, ambiguous pipeline status

technical_decisions.decision: Use interactive Claude Code session (not headless agent container) for requirements gathering
technical_decisions.rationale: The issue explicitly states pre-refine should be 'interactive and conversational (free-form back-and-forth, not structured HITL checkboxes)'. The existing _launch_claude() pattern in sdlc_hitl.py provides exactly this. A headless agent container cannot support real-time human conversation.
alternatives_considered: Multi-turn HITL decision loop — rejected: too rigid, not conversational
Headless agent with periodic HITL pauses — rejected: breaks conversational flow

technical_decisions.rationale: Follows the existing draft management pattern (analysis.md for refine, plan.md for plan). The identifier is the issue number (issue mode) or pipeline ID (local mode). The file is committed to the feature branch for auditability.
alternatives_considered: Store in issue body only — rejected: no artifact for local mode, no separate file for the refine agent to read
Store in contract JSON — rejected: requirements are prose, not structured data

technical_decisions.decision: Pre-refine is skippable via configuration (skip_pre_refine: true)
technical_decisions.rationale: Well-defined issues don't need requirements gathering. The skip flag lets the pipeline start directly at REFINE for: (1) issues that already have clear requirements, (2) headless/CI triggers where interactive sessions are impossible, (3) re-runs where requirements were already gathered. Default is false (pre-refine enabled).
alternatives_considered: Always require pre-refine — rejected: adds friction for well-defined issues
Auto-detect from issue quality — rejected: unreliable heuristic

technical_decisions.decision: In issue mode, update the GitHub issue description with approved requirements
technical_decisions.rationale: The issue states: 'In issue mode, the issue description on GitHub is updated with the approved requirements document.' This ensures the issue body is the canonical source of requirements. The original issue body is preserved (e.g., in a collapsed section) for context.
alternatives_considered: Post as a comment — rejected: refine agent reads the issue body, not comments
Only store in .egg-state file — rejected: issue description would be stale

technical_decisions.decision: No codebase interaction during pre-refine — Claude has no access to repository files
technical_decisions.rationale: The issue explicitly states: 'No codebase interaction — purely requirements-focused.' The Claude session should be configured without repository access to prevent scope creep into analysis. The refine agent handles codebase research.
alternatives_considered: Allow read-only codebase access — rejected: violates issue requirement, blurs line between pre-refine and refine

technical_decisions.decision: The pre-refine orchestrator phase immediately pauses (AWAITING_HUMAN) rather than spawning a container
technical_decisions.rationale: Pre-refine is human-driven. The orchestrator's role is to track state and wait, not to run an agent. The interactive Claude session is launched by the CLI (client-side), not the orchestrator (server-side). This matches the existing HITL pattern where the CLI handles human interaction.
alternatives_considered: Spawn a container that runs an interactive session — rejected: containers are non-interactive in the current architecture (--print mode)

risks.description: PRE_REFINE enum value requires updating all phase-handling code paths
risks.mitigation: Enumerate all switch/match/if-else chains on PipelinePhase across the codebase. Use grep for PipelinePhase, 'refine', and phase string comparisons. Most code paths can default pre-refine to the same behavior as refine (same permissions, same visualization style).

risks.description: Interactive Claude session may not work in all deployment modes (e.g., headless CI)
risks.mitigation: skip_pre_refine defaults to true in headless/CI mode (--print flag). The pre-refine phase is only interactive when a TTY is available via the egg-sdlc CLI.

risks.description: Requirements document quality depends on human engagement
risks.mitigation: Claude's system prompt should guide the conversation with probing questions. The refine agent still performs its own analysis, so pre-refine is additive quality improvement, not a replacement for analysis.

risks.description: Backward compatibility with existing pipelines that don't have PRE_REFINE state
risks.mitigation: Existing pipelines in REFINE state continue to work. Phase transition validation accepts REFINE as a starting phase. Only new pipelines start at PRE_REFINE (when not skipped). Pipeline state deserialization handles missing pre_refine phase execution gracefully.

risks.description: Claude session crash or disconnect during requirements gathering loses work
risks.mitigation: Claude writes to the requirements file incrementally during the conversation. Even if the session crashes, partial work is saved. The pipeline remains in PRE_REFINE/AWAITING_HUMAN state, so the human can resume by reattaching to the pipeline.

risks.description: Issue body update in issue mode may conflict with concurrent edits
risks.mitigation: The issue body update happens atomically via gh issue edit after approval. Concurrent editing of issue bodies during SDLC pipeline execution is unlikely. If it occurs, the last write wins (standard GitHub behavior).

constraints: Pre-refine must be purely conversational — no structured HITL checkboxes for requirements gathering
No codebase interaction during pre-refine — Claude should not access repository files
Must work in both issue mode and local mode
Must be skippable for well-defined issues and headless CI execution
In issue mode, GitHub issue description is updated with approved requirements
Human must explicitly approve before advancing to refine
Backward compatible: existing pipelines without pre-refine continue to function
The approved requirements document becomes the direct input to the refine phase, replacing the original issue body/prompt

open_questions.question: Should the requirements-gathering Claude session have read-only access to the repo structure (file listing) to help the human identify relevant areas?
open_questions.recommendation: No — the issue explicitly says 'no codebase interaction'. Keep pre-refine purely requirements-focused. The human can mention files/areas in conversation if needed.
open_questions.impact: Low — can be added later if needed

open_questions.question: Should the requirements document follow a strict template or be free-form?
open_questions.recommendation: Guide with a suggested structure (problem statement, functional requirements, constraints, acceptance criteria) but allow deviation. Claude's system prompt suggests the structure; the human can override.
open_questions.impact: Low — template can be refined based on usage

open_questions.question: Should pre-refine be the default for all new pipelines, or opt-in?
open_questions.recommendation: Default ON for interactive CLI usage, default OFF for headless/CI. The --skip-pre-refine flag provides an explicit opt-out for users who know their requirements are clear.

open_questions.question: How should the original issue body be preserved when updated with requirements in issue mode?
open_questions.recommendation: Include the original issue body in a collapsed <details> section at the bottom of the requirements document. This preserves context while making the requirements the primary content.
